subject: Clarify BAA applicability for audio webhook + transcription flow
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@wellspringhealth.com>, Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@wellspringhealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify BAA applicability for audio webhook + transcription flow

Hi Elena / Kevin,

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick clarification request from the engineering side so we can scope a potential BAA correctly. Your integration pattern described was: patient audio captured in-app => short-lived upload to WellSpring S3 => WellSpring posts audio to an HTTP webhook on Redwood for streaming transcription => Redwood returns transcript (and optional redaction metadata) to your callback URL.

Couple of specific questions that determine PHI scope on our side:
- Do the audio recordings ever contain patient identifiers in the audio itself (e.g., name, DOB, MRN)?
- Should the full raw audio blob be considered retained by Redwood after transcription, or is it deleted immediately after processing?
- Are you planning to send follow-up metadata (patient_id) alongside the webhook, or will the webhook be correlation-only (session id) with patient mapping kept on your side?

From our side we offer three operational patterns (we can provide a BAA for any of these, but scope changes):
1) Hosted streaming (default): transient processing; transcripts may be cached for short periods for retry.
2) Dedicated capacity: isolated GPU pool + configurable retention.
3) Private deployment (VPC / on-prem): Redwood control plane separate; no hosted storage of PHI.

If you can answer the three bullets above and let us know which deployment model you prefer, I’ll have security draft the minimal BAA scope and list required artifacts (SOC 2, DPIA notes). I attached a quick dataflow diagram and a sample webhook payload to make this concrete.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Tuesday or Thursday to walk the scope and confirm retention defaults.

Thanks,
Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mobile: 415-555-0198

Attachments: dataflow-edge-diagram.png, transcription_payload_example.json
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@wellspringhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify BAA applicability for audio webhook + transcription flow

Monica — thanks for the clear summary and attachments. A few clarifications from our legal/compliance side before we schedule:

- Audio content: yes, recordings can include patient name and short demographic phrases (we do not purposely include MRNs).
- Retention intent: We currently store raw audio on our S3 for up to 24 hours for replay/resync; transcripts are persisted in our database indefinitely unless flagged for deletion.
- Payloads: Right now we send patient_id with the webhook (we need correlation on our side).

High-level asks from WellSpring for the BAA draft:
- Explicit confirmation that Redwood will not use PHI for training or model improvement.
- Options for on-ingest pseudonymization and field-level redaction (we may request dynamic redaction of names).
- Evidence: SOC 2 report (most recent) and a short write-up of incident response timelines.

We prefer to aim for dedicated or private deployment; legal will confirm which after we see the retention controls. Can you also share an example subpoena/incident log redaction workflow?

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Legal & Compliance, WellSpring Health
elena.ruiz@wellspringhealth.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@wellspringhealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify BAA applicability for audio webhook + transcription flow

Elena — great, thanks for the details. Quick answers inline and next steps: 

- Training usage: Redwood will not use any customer-supplied PHI to train models unless explicitly contracted and mutually agreed in writing. We'll add that clause to the BAA.
- On-ingest pseudonymization: we support two patterns: client-side pseudonymization before sending (recommended) or server-side redaction filters (name/date patterns) that run prior to persistence. Server-side redaction can be enabled per-tenant in Dedicated/Private.
- Retention: hosted streaming may retain short caches (minutes) for retry; Dedicated gives you retention config down to hours; Private gives you full control / no hosted copies.

Attachments included: redaction-options.md (lists filters and regex patterns) and the dataflow diagram shows where redaction would run. I also attached a sample transcription payload (transcription_payload_example.json) with the fields we would store by default.

Proposed call times (PDT): Tuesday 5/11 10:00–10:30 or Thursday 5/13 09:00–09:30.

If Dedicated or Private looks necessary I’ll loop in Sales (Aditya) to get pricing/lead times and Security (Mina) to prepare a BAA draft and SOC 2 attestation summary.

Thanks,
Monica
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify BAA applicability for audio webhook + transcription flow

Monica / Aditya — quick security note for the thread:

Recommended minimum for WellSpring given they send patient_id and audio with names: 
- Move to Dedicated or Private (Private preferred for regulated PHI across multiple environments).
- Enforce server-side redaction/pseudonymization on ingest for any hosted transit cases (regex name scrubbing + optional NER-based redaction).
- Short retention defaults: raw audio TTL = 24h max, transcript TTL configurable (default 90 days) — set in BAA as negotiable.
- Contractual commitments: add 'no training on customer data' clause; require a 24-hour notification SLA for confirmed incidents.

I will prepare a BAA skeleton and SOC 2 summary; Aditya please coordinate pricing and provisioning windows for Private. Monica — please share any DPIA artifacts they may need; Elena asked about DPIA specifics.

-Mina
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@wellspringhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@wellspringhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify BAA applicability for audio webhook + transcription flow

Thanks — that all helps. WellSpring would like to pursue Private deployment to eliminate hosted copies. Two quick asks before we lock calendar: 
1) Please send the BAA draft and the SOC 2 PDF (redacted ok) to legal@wellspringhealth.com.
2) For DPIA intake: can you confirm the export controls for redaction metadata (we need to document any PII fields that are stored for audit) and provide the estimated retention config we can capture in the DPIA (e.g., transcript TTL options).

We’ll take the call 5/13 at 09:00 PDT. I’ll invite our engineering lead if needed.

Best,
Elena
